HANOI, Oct 31 : Vietnam will cut its average retail electricity price by 2 per cent and remove its special consumption tax on gasoline from November 1 to support economic stability and reduce costs for households and businesses, the government said on Saturday. • The average retail tariff will fall to 2,159.9 dong ($0.085) per kilowatt-hour, excluding value-added tax, the government said in a statement • Its special consumption tax on gasoline will be cut to zero from 7 per cent-10 per cent from November 1 until the end of March next year • The decision was intended to help maintain macroeconomic stability while supporting social welfare and business activity, it said • Vietnam targets an economic growth of above 10 per cent this year, and fourth-quarter growth must be higher than 12.5 per cent to meet that target

Source: Reuters

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Lewis Hamilton put Ferrari on pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix on Saturday with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli set to line up fourth on the grid for a ground-breaking race likely to make him Formula One's youngest champion at 20 years old. Antonelli needs only a ninth-place finish at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday to become Italy's first champion since 1953. He was fifth fastest in qualifying but will move up a place due to Red Bull's Max Verstappen, in fourth, taking a grid drop. The pole was a record-extending 105th of Hamilton's career and the Briton's first for Ferrari. "Thank you so much, it has been such a long time coming," Hamilton said over the team radio. "Mega job, guys - I am so grateful for the hard work you guys put in."

OLDEST POLE SITTER SINCE 1982 The last time he took pole in a regular grand prix, not including sprint races, was in Hungary in July 2023 - a wait of 1,197 days. It also made the seven-times world champion, 41, the oldest pole sitter since American Mario Andretti, at 42, in Italy in 1982. Mercedes' George Russell, Antonelli's closest rival but 123 points behind his teammate with only 100 to be won after this weekend, was second fastest and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc third. Both Hamilton and Russell have to win if either of the remaining contenders is to keep Antonelli waiting another week for the title. "I am happy. It has been a tricky few races for me and I'm still struggling to get on top of this car, to be honest," said Russell.  McLaren's Lando Norris, the reigning champion and last year's winner in Mexico, qualified sixth with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar seventh. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson was eighth fastest but also has a one-place grid drop for the clash with Verstappen in Friday practice. That will mean he starts ninth with teammate Arvid Lindblad eighth and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completing the top 10 on the grid. PIASTRI FAILS TO MAKE TOP 10 Antonelli was only seventh in the second phase, with Norris fastest and teammate Oscar Piastri knocked out in 13th place in a blow for McLaren's hopes of edging back in front of Red Bull in the battle for third overall. The Australian complained of lack of rear grip after being told he was out of the top 10. Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso halted the first session when the team told him to stop in the stadium section with a suspected water pressure issue in the power unit. The Spaniard was then noted for a general safety incident after he failed to reattach the steering wheel after getting out of the car. Hamilton was fastest in that first session, with Antonelli only ninth. Japanese Ryo Hirakawa, making his F1 race debut this weekend at the age of 32 and in place of Esteban Ocon, qualified 19th for Haas. Mexican Sergio Perez, preparing for his 300th grand prix in front of his home crowd, and Cadillac teammate Valtteri Bottas filled the back row.

Source: Reuters

MILAN, Oct 31 : AC Milan's Diego Moreira claimed one goal and two assists as his side took local bragging rights and three precious points with a 3-1 victory over Inter Milan in their Serie A clash on Saturday, while AS Roma enjoyed a 5-2 victory at Udinese. In a week when Milan and Inter announced they would build a new shared 71,500-seater stadium to replace the San Siro, Milan’s fast start earned the win that lifts them into fourth place, four points behind leaders Lazio and Inter who have 25. The result means Lazio can move three points clear of Inter when they host Cagliari on Sunday. Roma are third on 24 points. Milan made the perfect start as Christian Pulisic headed their opener after four minutes before Adrien Rabiot added a second six minutes later. Inter pulled a goal back through Alessandro Bastoni in the 22nd and the momentum was with them.

The next goal was always going to be crucial and it went to Milan as Moreira scored with a superb free-kick just before halftime to help his side to a fourth straight win over Inter. Roma were 4-0 up in 37 minutes at Udinese as they overwhelmed the hosts, who are second-bottom on five points. Bryan Cristante headed the first goal after 10 minutes, before Matias Soule and Donyell Malen struck the woodwork. Rodrigo Mora netted the second in the 31st minute after being set up by Cristante, and two minutes later Malen scored his eighth Serie A goal of the season. Evan Ndicka headed the fourth from a corner before halftime after which Udinese mounted something of a comeback. Nicolo Zaniolo and Matteo Palma scored for the hosts but Daniele Ghilardi added a fifth, his first Serie A goal, for Roma. "If we play like this there is a chance," Cristante said. "The league is not easy and it's nice to stay in (the title race). We are scoring a lot and that is very important," . Bologna climbed to ninth with a third successive league win thanks to a 2-1 victory over Monza, their first home success since April. Tommaso Pobega and Federico Bernardeschi netted for Bologna, after the visitors converted an early penalty through Gustavo Varela, the top Serie A scorer with nine goals in as many games. He had been substituted by the time Monza were awarded a second penalty in the final 10 minutes and this time Patrick Cutrone missed from the spot as they were denied a point.

Source: Reuters

Oct 31 : Barcelona enjoyed an emphatic 6-1 home win over Alaves on Saturday, with Raphinha, Fermin Lopez, Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon all on the scoresheet, as the hosts responded after losses to Real Madrid and Paris St Germain. Barca top LaLiga on 30 points, two ahead of Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0 earlier on Saturday, with Real Madrid six points off the pace before visiting Racing Santander on Sunday. The opening exchanges at Camp Nou were punctuated by frustrated shouts from home manager Hansi Flick in response to Barcelona's defending, but Alaves found it impossible to live with their fluid attacking play. After Pedri's pass sliced through the Alaves midfield, Fermin crossed for Raphinha to open the scoring in the eighth minute.

A brief Alaves reaction put the hosts under pressure but once Fermin netted from a tight angle in the 23rd minute, the game was one-way traffic in Barcelona's favour. Tenacious and incisive throughout, Fermin assisted Raphinha again in the 41st minute after winning possession back. Lamine rifled a bouncing ball low into the corner to complete a slick passing move, adding Barcelona's fourth in first-half stoppage time. Flick's side continued to look sharp and Karim Adeyemi spurned a chance to round off more excellent work from Fermin early in the second half. Lamine was then set up by substitute Gabriel Jesus for his second in the 64th minute. Rodri was visibly delighted with the weight of his pass behind the Alaves defence, which Anthony Gordon converted for Barcelona's fifth with nine minutes remaining. The Spain midfielder was equally furious with himself after his giveaway allowed Mariano Diaz to add a consolation goal for Alaves three minutes later. Barca showed the verve they were missing in the 2-1 Clasico defeat by visitors Real, after which Flick said his team lacked freshness, and a 4-2 loss at PSG in the Champions League. Aston Villa visit the Catalan side on Tuesday in the Champions League in what is likely to be a sterner test.

Source: Reuters

Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday (Oct 31) it has been able to replace 90 per cent of the amount stolen after a record US$6.3 billion hack of its platform by using company money to buy new tokens. The remaining 10 per cent consists of tokens that are less liquid, meaning they may take longer to buy, it said in a statement posted on X. "We've now replenished 90 per cent of the stolen assets, and we're committed to covering the remaining 10 per cent. Our users will not bear the financial impact of this incident," co-CEO Richard Teng said on X on Saturday. Crypto prices fell on Friday, while Binance — the world's biggest crypto exchange — sought to reassure customers that their funds were safe after losing more than US$6 billion worth of crypto in a hack that analysts and the FBI blamed on North Korea.

The FBI on Saturday said the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Members of the unit were observed by law enforcement converting stolen assets into the cryptocurrency ethereum, the FBI said in a statement, adding that it expects "further laundering" of the assets through the use of related technology. Teng said on Friday that the breach was a "complex attack" involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate.

Related:

Gone in 20 minutes: How the biggest heist in crypto history unfolded

After the hack, the exchange stopped allowing customers to withdraw their funds, but it said on Saturday it was still on track to reopen withdrawals on Sunday. Binance said it has set aside around US$6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its US$1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company's own corporate treasury, it said on X. Binance also said it had taken a new snapshot of assets held on its platform as of midnight on October 31, as part of its proof-of-reserves process. Users holding the 10 listed tokens — BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC — would be able to verify that their assets were backed at a minimum ratio of 1:1 once the full proof was available, it said.

LONDON, Oct 31 : Oliver Glasner said he could become the fifth manager to be sacked by Nottingham Forest in little over a year if he did not turn around the club's dismal start to the season. Forest went down 2-0 at Brentford on Saturday to stay in the bottom three with one win from their opening nine Premier League games and Glasner said change was needed. "We have to accept it's not good enough," Glasner, who enjoyed great success at Crystal Palace in the last two seasons before moving to the City Ground, told a press conference. "If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do."

Forest have churned through managers since Nuno Espirito Santo parted company with the club last September, since when Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira have all come and gone. "I feel I could see a few things from day number one. I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises," Glasner said. "It's a clear way. I will tell (the players) what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround and, if not, the sixth manager (since the start of last season) will come in." Asked if he was concerned about his future, Austrian Glasner said: "I have no consequences. For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family. It's not the worst situation. Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner or with the manager. "If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won't do it. But, you know, the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it's the same, sorry for the word, shit situation that the club had last year. "So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises. Zero. Zero. And if these things don't work, they will let me know. "I didn't come to Nottingham because I was bored at home. No, I came to Nottingham to succeed. I came to Nottingham to get the visions of the owner and the fans and the club to reality. And therefore we need to have a bigger change than maybe I thought, to be honest." Glasner also said he did not need to "be loved" by his players and that he had turned down a request from one player to travel back from London alone. "I was asked if a player can drive home alone. I said no," Glasner said. "I have no understanding (why) somebody wants to go home on his own today, from London to Nottingham. No, go with the bus like everybody else. No extras. No extras."

Source: Reuters

Oct 31 : Real Madrid defender Eder Militao's house was burgled during his side's 2-1 victory over Barcelona on Sunday, with El Mundo reporting on Saturday that thieves took jewellery and watches valued at €350,000 ($391,000). The Brazilian was on the bench for Real Madrid when thieves entered his home through a third-floor bathroom window and ransacked Militao's bedroom. Bags, watches and jewellery were stolen. Militao's family were in the house watching the Clasico match on the ground floor and did not notice anything suspicious. The burglary was the latest in a series targeting high-profile footballers in Spain in recent years.

MUNICH, Oct 31 : Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for Bayern Munich as Borussia Dortmund snatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw in a thrilling Klassiker on Saturday that kept the teams level on points at the top. In a frustrating match for home fans, Bayern twice took the lead, missed a penalty, hit the post four times and had three players - Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise - taken off injured. The Bavarians play Atletico Madrid in the Champions League next week. Kane, who claimed his prize at a ceremony in London on Monday, was an unused substitute in the 6-1 German Cup second-round demolition of Magdeburg on Wednesday before missing from the spot with Bayern 1-0 up. Silva snatched the equaliser in the 89th minute to leave both teams on 18 points, with Bayern top on goal difference.

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Reigning champion Lando Norris was fastest on Saturday in final practice for a Mexico City Grand Prix set to crown 20-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli as Formula One's youngest title winner. The McLaren driver put in a flying late lap of one minute 17.600 seconds at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez to top the timesheets by the slimmest of margins, 0.001 faster than Antonelli who is poised to become Italy's first F1 world champion since 1953. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, fastest in both Friday sessions, was third quickest and 0.117 off the pace, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri fourth. Red Bull's four-times champion Max Verstappen, who has a one place grid drop for Sunday's race, was fifth fastest ahead of Ferrari's seven-times champion Lewis Hamilton.

By Rohith Nair Oct 31 : MotoGP is set to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix even as a group of riders demand more assurances for travelling to the region, with organisers arguing that a "zero-risk environment" is unrealistic. The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to November 6-8 due to the regional conflict.

"MotoGP has provided teams and riders with every assurance available from the State of Qatar, the circuit... and our own ongoing risk assessment processes," a MotoGP spokesperson told Reuters. "We fully respect the concerns raised and highlight that safety remains the priority for everyone involved." However, the spokesperson said the expectation of a zero-risk environment was not realistic anywhere in the world by any government or organiser. "Over the past months, we have maintained continuous dialogue with teams and riders, sharing the latest information available, providing direct access to documents and answering questions openly and transparently." Carlos Ezpeleta, deputy CEO of MotoGP, visited Qatar on Thursday where the circuit's president Abdulrahman Al-Mannai said they were ready to welcome the riders, teams and fans for the 20th round of the season. However, Spain's embassy in Qatar has issued a notice urging its citizens not to travel to the Gulf nation unless it was absolutely necessary. Spaniards make up the largest share of riders on the grid, including world champion Marc Marquez. EVACUATION PLAN IN PLACE A MotoGP source said Qatar has guaranteed teams would not be stranded in case of escalation in the conflict and they could leave the country safely in time for the final two rounds in Portugal and Spain later in November. "Additional impossible asks at the last moment go beyond what can realistically be guaranteed by any event organiser, government or sporting body," the spokesperson added. "Our position is based solely on the most up-to-date intelligence, expert advice and assurances available to us." RIDERS SEEK ASSURANCES The source said championship leader Marquez, a seven-times MotoGP champion, was one of the riders seeking more assurances. Marquez has not publicly stated his position on travelling to Qatar but Ducati team manager Davide Tardozzi defended the Spaniard after he came under criticism for not taking a stance. "I have read that all the blame has been placed on Marc, as if he were the one who did not want to go to Qatar. That is not the case," he told Sky Sport. "Marc simply asked, as many other riders did, for an organisational safety plan - nothing more, nothing less. He did not say, 'I don't want to go'. "There are circumstances that could make you think it would be better not to go. But if the necessary safety conditions are in place, including an evacuation plan and guarantees that there will be no problems if something happens, then we will go." Reuters has contacted Ducati and Marquez for comment. APRILIA KEEN TO RACE IN QATAR Aprilia are keen to race in Qatar with Spanish rider Jorge Martin, second in the standings behind Marquez after withdrawing from the Malaysian Grand Prix due to a wrist injury. "We need to turn the page and look to the next chapter, Qatar, hoping it goes better, and keep this fight going to the last," Aprilia's technical director Fabiano Sterlacchini said. "This setback has certainly made things harder for us." The MotoGP source confirmed that no decision has been taken about sporting sanctions if teams or riders do not participate in Qatar.

Source: Reuters

Oct 31 : Manchester City slumped to their second Premier League defeat in a row on Saturday, going down 1-0 at home to third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion thanks to an early goal by Yasin Ayari. City could be knocked off their perch at the top of the table if Arsenal get at least a point at Liverpool on Sunday. The defeat was City's first at home by Brighton in the Premier League, and though Enzo Maresca's side managed 21 shots on goal, only six were on target and none managed to beat keeper Bart Verbruggen.  "Unbelievable feeling. We go 1-0 up and then to hang tight, the last 30-40 minutes we completely lost control of the game," Verbruggen told Sky Sports.

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar was given a formal warning on Saturday after he pushed away a Formula One guest in the Mexico City Grand Prix paddock. • The Frenchman was hurrying to first practice on Friday but stopped to have a photograph with a young fan when he was approached by a man in what stewards, who summoned Hadjar to a hearing, said was an "aggressive manner". • "One security person was walking behind him and was unable to intervene and prevent what was tantamount to an invasion of the driver's private space," the stewards said. • "The driver initially resisted the move by placing his hand on the waist of the guest, holding him at bay, then the driver pushed him aside with his open right hand." • The stewards said Hadjar was in breach of the regulations but considered various factors in mitigation, including that the action was uninvited and aggressive, that the driver did not have sufficient security and that others had experienced issues in moving through the paddock.

Oct 31 : Fakhar Zaman's superb century powered Pakistan to a three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-Day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday, ending the hosts' long wait for the title. Zaman's 127 off 99 balls anchored the chase after an early wobble, while Salman Agha provided crucial support before Arafat Minhas' half-century paved the way for victory. Pakistan chasing down a target of 326, finished on 331 with nine balls to spare to complete the joint-highest successful chase in an ODI final. Earlier, Sri Lanka posted a formidable 325 for eight wickets, built around Kamindu Mendis' outstanding 131 off 128 balls and a fluent 77 from Pavan Rathnayake. The pair shared a crucial 146-run partnership before Pakistan struck late to curb any hopes of a 340-plus surge, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking two wickets for 50 runs.

The victory secured Pakistan's first ODI tri-series title since 2008, when they beat India in the Kitply Cup final in Bangladesh, and made amends for their defeat to New Zealand in the final of a home tri-series in 2025. Pakistan suffered early setbacks as Dilshan Madushanka struck twice in the powerplay, including the prized wicket of Babar Azam for a five-ball duck. Zaman and Saad Baig rebuilt the innings with an impressive 149-run partnership and Baig brought up his maiden ODI fifty before Maheesh Theekshana ended his knock for 74 off 75 balls. Zaman accelerated after reaching his half-century and went on to register his 12th ODI century, partnering with Agha in a brisk 57-run stand that kept Pakistan firmly on course in the chase. The left-hander eventually fell to Madushanka, followed soon by Agha for 17, leaving Pakistan at 230-5. However, Minhas' and Hasan Nawaz's 94-run partnership ultimately carried the hosts to the target. Sri Lanka made a strong start after being put in to bat, with opener Avishka Fernando and Kamindu Mendis adding 51 runs in the powerplay. Fernando's dismissal in the 18th over ended the opening stand, and Pakistan struck again soon after when captain Kusal Mendis fell to Agha, leaving the visitors at 109-2. Kamindu and Rathnayake steadied the innings with a fluent 146-run partnership off 119 deliveries. The stand kept Sri Lanka firmly in control until Kamindu, who brought up his maiden ODI century, fell after hitting 12 fours and two sixes. Pakistan fought back in the death overs, triggering a collapse as Afridi and Haris Rauf removed Dasun Shanaka and Rathnayake within the space of two overs. Sahan Arachchige provided a late cameo with a brisk 15 off 12 deliveries before falling to Naseem Shah.

LONDON, Oct 31 : Manchester United's nightmare winless run reached nine games when they lost 2-0 at Chelsea and Manchester City also suffered a harrowing Halloween as the Premier League leaders went down 1-0 at home to Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday. United were the better team before halftime at Stamford Bridge but paid heavily for not taking chances as a solo effort by Morgan Rogers and a Cole Palmer penalty after the break heaped more pressure on the visitors' manager Michael Carrick. A horror start to the second half for United was compounded by a needless red card for defender Lisandro Martinez in conceding the 63rd-minute penalty that Palmer tucked away. United were spared dropping into the relegation zone only by virtue of Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace both losing - 2-0 at Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur respectively.

City's 100 per cent Premier League record was ended last week by Aston Villa and their hopes of bouncing back quickly were undone by third-placed Brighton who avenged their midweek League Cup loss to City thanks to Yasin Ayari's early goal. FOREST'S POOR FORM CONTINUES Champions Arsenal will replace City as leaders if they avoid defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. City have 21 points from nine games with Arsenal also on 21 from eight, Brighton on 19 and Chelsea in fourth place on 16. Coventry City moved out of the relegation zone as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni were on target in a 3-1 home win over Sunderland who are bottom. Bournemouth beat Leeds United 2-0 to move seventh with Evanilson netting for the fourth successive league game while Forest remain in the bottom three as their poor form under new manager Oliver Glasner continued with defeat at Brentford making it five league games without a win. The battle between two of the promoted sides ended honours even as Hull City drew 2-2 at home to Ipswich Town and in the late game Aston Villa drew 1-1 at home with Fulham after their keeper Zion Suzuki fumbled a corner into his own net. Carrick has now overseen United's longest winless run since 1988 and a fourth successive Premier League defeat means they have just seven points from their opening nine games. Despite the stark statistics, Carrick was warmly applauded by the travelling fans after the final whistle. Bruno Fernandes returned to the starting line-up as captain after being benched for last week's defeat at Bournemouth for his critical comments about the team, and United were rejuvenated as they enjoyed the better of the first half. Things could have been so different had Matheus Cunha's goal been allowed to stand or a host of opportunities been taken, including Amad firing over when looking odds on to score. United's good work unravelled after the break, however, with defender Martinez, who also criticised the club's hierarchy, most culpable. After Rogers strolled through unopposed to dink in Chelsea's opener, Martinez received two yellow cards in three minutes, the second for inexplicably pushing his arm into the face of Wesley Fofana at a corner, to concede the penalty. "I think I take away a lot of the positives from the first half," Carrick said.  "But the game unravelled and got away from us. It's happened too often really so we've got to learn from that and we've got to do something about it pretty quickly." NO GOALS FOR CITY DESPITE 21 ATTEMPTS City had done an impressive job of ignoring the dark clouds hanging over the club after an independent commission found them guilty of 114 out of 115 financial charges but after winning their opening seven Premier League games, Enzo Maresca's side have hit the buffers. They fell behind in the 11th minute when a miscued clearance by Matheus Nunes fell for Ayari who converted from close range. City poured on the pressure in search of an equaliser but Brighton, who had led twice against City in the League Cup, produced a textbook away display to hang on to the points. The hosts had 21 goal attempts but failed to score for the first time in 25 Premier League matches. Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton side have now beaten Arsenal and City this season and while they have been free-scoring, they showed another side on Saturday. "There's an old phrase - defence wins you battles and wins you championships. Of course, we're not speaking about the championship, but especially today we needed to have this defensive mindset. It's always a togetherness when you defend like we did," Hurzeler said. Resurgent Tottenham made it three wins on the bounce to move eighth although they were given a helping hand as Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was red-carded in the 13th minute for a lunging tackle on Micky van de Ven. Archie Gray headed Spurs in front after 25 minutes and Jan Paul van Hecke wrapped it up with a header from a prone position after his initial effort hit the bar.

Source: Reuters
